description: Two REAL OCI images for the containers module's PEEL + Diff-the-Trace legs. The 'clean' twin is stock alpine:latest (arm64v8) straight off Docker Hub; the 'misconfigured' twin is a real `docker build` over it that adds the control-truth the module diagnoses — User root, ExposedPorts 22+8080, an expanded Env, and a SECOND layer whose tar bakes in a test AWS credential. Every region the PEEL surface shows is read by web/src/engines/visual/oci.ts straight from these committed real blobs; the discriminating field in each diff is the parser's computed divergence, never an answer key.

provenance.captured_with: clean: `docker pull alpine:latest && docker save alpine:latest` (OCI-layout tarball), arm64v8 manifest sha256:74e11dac… → config sha256:92385f4b…. misconfigured: a real `docker build` (buildkit) from the Dockerfile committed below, then `docker save`, image manifest sha256:7869dc00… → config sha256:2cd49630… with layers c05efffa… (stock rootfs) + 48092d72… (the secret layer).
provenance.cross_checked_against: docker inspect / docker save output, and the content-addressable digest chain itself: each manifest cites its config and layers by sha256:<hex>, and those digests equal the recomputed SHA-256 of the committed blobs (verified locally with shasum -a 256 and by web/tests/oci-fidelity.test.ts via crypto.subtle). skopeo was unavailable on the capture host; docker inspect/save is the equivalent reference reader and the digest recompute is the stronger check (it cannot pass on a tampered blob).
provenance.honesty_note: The 'clean' twin is the upstream stock image, NOT a fully-hardened one — stock alpine has no explicit User, which per the OCI runtime default means it too runs as root; the parser reports that honestly ('absent → defaults to root'). The teaching contrast in the diff is the set of findings the misconfigured build ADDS (exposed ports, an expanded Env, a real secret-bearing second layer), each a genuine on-disk fact. The baked credential is a documented AWS *example* key (…CYEXAMPLEKEY), not a live secret, but it is really written into the real layer tar — exactly the antipattern. Nothing is invented; anyone can `docker save` the same tags and recompute the identical digests.

misconfigured.label: real `docker build` twin (root, exposed ports, baked secret)

map.comment: The findings→controls + VM-vs-container board (module 21 MAP leg). Each item's keyZone is the cited authoritative control/definition the finding maps to; mapping_correct reads placedZone === keyZone. Control key cited to CIS Docker Benchmark + NIST SP 800-190 + NIST 800-53; VM/container key cited to vendor-neutral virtualization definitions. The findings themselves are read off the real manifest/config by the oci oracle — only the control mapping is the cited key.

items.label: Virtual machine (hardware-virtualized guest)
items.keyRef: NIST 800-190 §2.1 (VM = own guest kernel; container = shared host kernel)

items.label: Container (namespace/cgroup isolation)
items.keyRef: NIST 800-190 §2.1 / §2.3 (containers share the host kernel — a larger blast radius)

diff_pairs.control_claim: containers do not run as root (CM-6 / NIST 800-190 / CIS Docker 4.1)
diff_pairs.note: Both stock alpine and the twin run as root; the twin makes it explicit (User: root). The hardened ideal is an explicit non-root uid. The parser reads the real User field in each.

diff_pairs.control_claim: only the service port is exposed (CM-7 least functionality)
diff_pairs.note: The misconfigured build EXPOSEs 22 (SSH) alongside the app port — the CM-7 finding the parser surfaces from ExposedPorts.

diff_pairs.control_claim: no secrets are baked into the image (IA-5 / SC-28 / CIS Docker 4.10)
diff_pairs.note: The parser walks the real layer tar and the secret-scanner pattern set trips on the real AWS-style credential in the second layer — the secret glows in the layer that added it, cited by its real digest.
